originality.rationale: A new complete first-Cartier rank and a-number computation for the cyclic scalar quotient, not the additive covering curve. The 2026 cover-image theorem is stronger on the covering object and is openly used; its published statement gives no quotient invariant. Tame invariant descent and the nontrivial odd-residue count supply the distinct formula. Primary full texts and published-finding corpus searches did not find the same all-parameter statement. Priority remains qualified by possible uninspected older quotient literature and the general covering theorem.
residual_risks: The formula is derived from a 2026 covering-curve image theorem by tame invariants; an unrecorded corollary or earlier computation may contain an equivalent quotient evaluation.

The 2005 Pries article Jacobians of quotients of Artin-Schreier curves was located only to abstract-level evidence; its full text was not inspected, although its described family and Newton-polygon aim differ.
The finite direct-matrix verifier specializes coefficients and cannot establish all-coefficient or infinite-parametric correctness; those rest on the published triangular minor and this proof.

value.rationale: The Jacobian a-number distinguishes finite group-scheme structures not fixed by maximality or supersingularity and supplies a previously unreported invariant for explicit new maximal curves with trivial automorphism groups in every odd characteristic. The same argument covers arbitrary even-support coefficient choices and yields a size-independent precise quotient defect. Nontrivial tame-isotypic extraction and parity counting are needed beyond the numerical cover rank; no broader Jacobian classification is claimed.
